title: Master Services Agreement (MSA) Standards and Contract Negotiation Framework

sections.section_title: 1. Standard Contract Terms and Governing Law
sections.content: All corporate commercial agreements, customer contracts, and vendor master services agreements (MSAs) must adopt the approved corporate standard legal templates. Governing law for US operations is the State of Delaware; for EMEA operations, governing law is the courts of England and Wales. Modifications to governing law require General Counsel sign-off.

sections.section_title: 2. Limitation of Liability and Indemnification Caps
sections.content: Corporate policy stipulates that aggregate liability under any commercial contract shall not exceed 12 months of total fees paid or payable by the customer under the applicable Order Form. Super-caps for data breach or gross negligence are restricted to a maximum of 2x the standard annual fee cap.

Mutual non-disclosure agreements (NDAs) must mandate confidentiality protection for a minimum period of 5 years following disclosure of proprietary business information. Trade secrets, source code, and customer records must be protected in perpetuity without expiration.

title: Global Data Privacy Regulation (GDPR & CCPA) Compliance Manual

sections.section_title: 1. Data Subject Access Requests (DSAR) Response Timelines
sections.content: Under GDPR Article 15 and California CCPA/CPRA regulations, verified Data Subject Access Requests (DSAR)—including requests to access, rectify, or delete personal data—must be fulfilled within 30 calendar days of identity verification. An extension of up to 60 additional days is permissible only for exceptionally complex requests upon written notification to the applicant.

sections.section_title: 2. Personal Data Breach Mandatory Notification Window
sections.content: In the event of a confirmed personal data security incident affecting employee or customer data, the Data Protection Officer must notify the lead supervisory data authority (e.g. Irish DPC or UK ICO) within 72 hours of becoming aware of the breach, pursuant to GDPR Article 33. Affected individuals must be notified without undue delay if the breach carries a high risk to personal freedoms.

Transfers of personal data originating from the European Economic Area (EEA) to third countries must rely upon valid Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) approved by the European Commission, accompanied by a documented Transfer Impact Assessment (TIA), or an EU-US Data Privacy Framework certification.
